headline: Advancements in Quantum Algorithms and Many-Body Simulation
summary: Today's research spans fundamental quantum complexity, advanced algorithms for arithmetic and optimization, and novel techniques for simulating complex many-body and fermionic systems. Together, these papers highlight continued progress in making quantum simulations and computations both more scalable and mathematically rigorous.

themes.title: Quantum Algorithms and Complexity
themes.body: New developments in quantum computation include query-optimal minimum finding from numerical estimators and highly efficient, in-place, ancilla-free quantum algorithms for integer multiplication and modular inversion.

themes.title: Quantum Many-Body Simulation
themes.body: Progress in simulating correlated quantum matter features neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states for large lattice systems and a dynamical averaging method to improve accuracy for neural-network quantum states.

themes.title: Quantum States and Superfluids
themes.body: Theoretical proofs show that high-temperature Gibbs states are uniformly Markovian and trivial, while experimental work maps 2D velocity fields and quantized vortices in atomic superfluids via local velocimetry.

connections.body: Both papers focus on advancing neural-network quantum states by either scaling tensor network simulations for strongly correlated fermions or introducing dynamical averaging to suppress observable errors.
